question: Why did Desktop Commander calls to octo-w01 and octo-l01 stop returning between roughly 21:20 and 21:50 UTC on 2026-10-12, while both devices still reported Online?

prompting_observation.text: you can't just [...] SAY this without understand[ing] WHY the thi[n]g that is supposed to helm the ENTIRE [...] ESTATE is sluggish and you're like.. oh well, let's go!

origin.author: repository owner (BigBirdReturns)
origin.note: Elisions marked [...] remove expletives only; bracketed letters correct typos. The session had labelled the device 'sluggish' and moved on; the owner refused the label without a cause.

competing_explanations.text: The session's own recursive directory walk over the whole 443 GB platter-backed D: Storage Spaces pool on octo-w01 (PowerShell PID 17236, started about 21:21 UTC) saturated disk I/O and starved the device agent.
competing_explanations.narrowed_by: Cannot be the primary cause: octo-l01, a different machine, timed out at 21:33 and failed a ping at 21:43, and a ping touches no disk. It may still have made w01 worse after 21:21.

evidence_for.text: w01 latency rose from about 20 s (21:20) to 103 s and repeated 120 s timeouts after 21:30.

evidence_against.text: ping to octo-l01 at 21:43:38 UTC: 'Timeout - no response from device'. ping to octo-w01 at 21:43:37: same.
22:00 UTC: latency on octo-l01 (ping 19 s) matched octo-w01 (ping 19 s) although only w01 carried the scan.

competing_explanations.text: The relay path between the cloud and the estate was slow or backlogged for every device.

evidence_for.text: Relay call log showed 50 s (21:08) and 26 s (21:14) latencies on w01 before this session ran anything; both devices failed pings; presence heartbeats still read Online and 'last seen 1m ago'.

21:59:51 UTC: pings sent to octo-w01 and octo-l01 in the same second; both completed at 22:00:10 within 0.3 s of each other after 19 s in flight. Simultaneous release on two machines is relay-side behaviour.

22:00:53 to 22:01:48 UTC: list_sessions and read_file on octo-w01 each took about 55 s with no other session's calls in the relay log since 21:45. Calls that overrun the 60 s synchronous window return status completed with no body, so their results are lost.

competing_explanations.text: At least three Claude sessions were queued on the same per-device agent, which appears to serve one call at a time, so each 120 s timeout held the queue for everyone.

evidence_for.text: list_remote_tool_calls showed read_multiple_files and read_file calls from other sessions pending on both devices at 21:32 to 21:35, and a stair-step pattern of one completion followed by several timeouts.

evidence_against.text: Relay call log 21:45 to 22:01 UTC: only this session's calls, each about 55 s.

competing_explanations.narrowed_by: Between 21:45 and 22:01 UTC the relay log showed no calls from other sessions, yet single calls still took 55 s. Contention from other sessions can lengthen the queue but is not what makes a lone call slow.

competing_explanations.text: Something estate-side was consuming the shared uplink, such as a Kopia backup under D:\Octo-Backup or a LocalAI model pull; octo-l01's LocalAI folder changed at 03:18 on 2026-10-12.

dispositions.reason: H1 narrowed to a contributor at most; H2, H3 and H4 remain live and need a device response to discriminate. The session stopped issuing reads, sent force_terminate for PID 17236 and stop_search for its ripgrep session; neither was acknowledged before this row was written.

The relay resumed around 22:00 UTC. Both devices released in the same second, a lone call still takes about 55 s, and overrunning calls lose their bodies. H2 (relay path) is the leading explanation; H1 and H3 are narrowed to contributors; H4 untested. Whether PID 17236 is still alive on w01 could not be read because the list_sessions body was lost.

locators.note: Estate status read at 21:22 UTC: ESTATE STATUS HOLD, observed 2026-09-09; W01 power-off HOLD.

next_examination.what: Measure a lone ping to each device every few minutes to see whether the 55 s latency is steady or decaying (H2); on octo-w01 run a single short list_sessions and kill PID 17236 if alive; check Kopia and LocalAI activity for 21:00 to 22:00 UTC on both machines (H4); raise with the relay operator that calls completing after the synchronous window return no body.

question: Did the M-04G global circulation workflow ever carry prior observations forward between runs, so that a change in a source could be detected?

question_origin.author: read-only survey agent spawned by session_01J1343QFCPd8NjT6o1gRk2R

prompting_observation.text: The workflow caches build/global-circulation/state, but the refresh tool writes state to <output-dir>/state/<basin>.json and output-dir is build/global-circulation/<basin>. So the cached directory is always empty, previous is always {}, and every orbit reports every poll as new_source_baseline or new_metadata_fingerprint.

competing_explanations.text: State persisted through the Actions cache and change detection worked as the milestone describes.

evidence_against.note: line 22 resolves --output-dir; line 58 writes state under <output-dir>/state/<basin>.json
cache restore and save used path build/global-circulation/state while --output-dir was build/global-circulation/<basin>

competing_explanations.text: The cache path and the refresh output path never matched, so no run ever saw a previous state.

dispositions.reason: Confirmed by reading both files. The workflow's cache paths were changed to build/global-circulation/<basin>/state in the same commit that adds this row. Whether change detection now works in a live run is not yet observed; the first scheduled orbit after the fix will show it.

next_examination.what: After the next scheduled orbit, read the orbit-manifest.json artifact for any basin and check that counts.new_source_baseline is no longer equal to counts.selected on the second run. The hydrology workflow has a sibling defect: freshwater and ocean jobs share a cache prefix and overwrite each other's state.
